RESULT (a2-bounded-arm-check-decision-20261023): B passed; C ran complete inside the budget and its calibration record is refused by its own stationarity check (descriptive evidence: the fit reproduces recorded arm poses at the numerical floor, at a measured 0.202 s per arm and start); the a2 preflight record and the two named Tests rows are written at the retained fingerprint 83ff9dd7eb5e2699; the world-flush wait is not a scheduling defect (analysis below). No binding, freezing, adoption or launch; the supervisor stays paused; no trainer runs.

1. --moment-video (item 1). Kept as a configuration flag: main's training_preflight.py (358bf4c7..., the unbound seventh entry applied, RUN_FLAGS unchanged) computes 83ff9dd7eb5e2699, and the preflight record's text states that reading. One inconsistency is left, reported rather than rebuilt: the source branch's own copy of training_preflight.py (commit 9ad987ef4) lists --moment-video in its RUN_FLAGS, and video_switches_check asserted that copy's reading; that copy is not the launch's checker and enters no fingerprint. Removing the line means a new source commit, so a new pinned HEAD and a package rebuild with the same fingerprint: yours to decide.

2. B. Tests row arm_pose_fit_tests_check PASS: 15 of 15 tests at c86363ae2, none skipped, pytest 38.1 s (whole command 46.65 s), the saved world read only.

3. C. Tests row arm_fit_calibration_check: complete (not partial), exit 0, the driver's own total 75.85 s, whole command 85.05 s; B plus C 131.70 s of the 900 s. Input: the saved seg40 world, 107 records, per arm 100 distinct poses with every hinge inside its range (of 12,716 left and 12,931 right offered) plus 7 past-range poses; geometry fingerprint 4bbc9289...
- Floor fits (started at the recorded angles: the numerical floor, not the live initial guess's reliability): 214 fits, 0 failures; largest residual 5.04e-6 cm and 9.14e-6 degrees; hinge angles recovered within 3.75e-7 rad (left) and 2.26e-6 rad (right).
- The record is REFUSED by its own pass line, check floor_fits_stationary (the other 12 checks pass): 33 of 100 left and 20 of 100 right floor fits are stationary; the flow ran its 400 iterations (median), and the final projected gradients (medians 1.44e-8 rad left, 1.55e-8 rad right) sit above the 1e-10 rad line. No lines exist; no check was relaxed.
- Locality (in sample, the reference start then the range middle): left, above on the 7 past-range poses only; right, above on 3 of the 100 inside poses and the 7 past-range poses. One of those 3 is above its line by 1.3e-9 cm (5.0426e-6 against 5.0412e-6 cm), at the floor's scale; one reference-start fit ended 2.41 rad from the recorded angles on one hinge (the record does not tie that fit to the 3).
- Past-range allowance: at most 0.0236 cm and 0.112 degrees. Coverage, each hinge's recorded span as a share of its range: elbows 0.96 and 0.98, shoulder rotation 0.95 and 0.90, shoulder horizontal 0.48 and 0.84, shoulder abduction 0.58 and 0.65, wrist hinges 0.24 to 0.44.
- Measured fit time per arm and start: median 0.202 s, 90th percentile 0.216 s (left) and 0.211 s (right).
- Smallest repair of the refusal (PROPOSED, not built): _Arm.project discards the L-BFGS-B result (limb_target_control.py 484-489); record its status, message, nit and nfev per start, and count a fit stationary when its flow settled or its kept polish ended on its own gtol or ftol stop (status 0); its computation would not change. Whether C's record would then pass is unknown until a rerun records the stop reasons. A fact beside it, not proven as the cause: rotmat_log takes the turn as arccos((trace - 1) / 2), so a nonzero turn reads at least 1.49e-8 rad, 149 times the 1e-10 line.

4. The arithmetic (item 4). In the design document (doc-only commit 212817d1a on repair/s4r-arm-ik-fk-2026-10-22): the stop-rate table is conditional arithmetic, valid only if forecasts and floor poses were exchangeable draws fitted under comparable conditions, which recorded poses, known-angle starts and learned forecasts do not establish; it is not a forecast of stop frequency; two local starts prove no impossibility, and fit_failed, a fit above its lines and a proven impossibility stay three different outcomes. The module's own constants comment (arm_pose_fit.py 157-165) keeps the earlier wording; changing it is a module change: yours to authorize.

5. The smallest practical connection to planner learning and selection (item 5; document section 7; all PROPOSED, none built, none uses lines, none writes a fitted pose into a forecast, score or command). Costs are ARITHMETIC on C's measured fit times.
- (a) OFFLINE DIAGNOSIS: after a run, fit the capture's durable iteration-0 and selected forecast poses (forecast_pose__*) from the measured hinge angles of the observer record the capture names, and report per forecast the residual per arm part, iteration 0 against selected, and whether larger residuals forecast the measured end pose worse. At most 16 forecasts x 0.405 s = 6.47 s per captured decision for the first fits. Needs a run with these arrays on disk (a2 would write them), a join driver and a Tests row. It is the smallest step that informs planner work without touching selection.
- (b) A RECORD-ONLY RUNTIME SCREEN of each body's selected forecast after the keep rule, with a time budget per decision: 3.24 s per decision in the trainer process (0.65 s per model step; 76 per 100 of the rate at 2.0 s per model step), or 0.428 s in the 8 world processes (96 per 100). Changes no eligibility. Before any eligibility use it needs: the residual distribution on forecasts, accepted lines with an exceedance rate measured on held-out poses, the screen's time on forecasts, and a count of the decisions a rule would have stopped.
- (c) A JOINT-CONSISTENT PREDICTOR: the body head outputs hinge-angle changes composed by a differentiable forward kinematics, or a consistency term on today's forecast poses; needs the arm geometry and a torch arm kinematics in the learner; it changes learning and is the largest.
- The earlier cost table underestimated this fit (its Sept 25 basis is 5.7 times below the measured median): fitting every forecast of a decision costs 68.0 s in one process and 8.98 s in the 8 world processes (13 and 53 per 100 of the training rate).

6. THE FINAL PACKAGE (item 6), for the next launch decision. Repair package D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/h84/d1_planner_recovery/s4r_pose_learning_496250_repair_package:
- the preflight record docs/gain_of_function_v4/preflight/83ff9dd7eb5e2699.json, sha256 74396481..., all seven gates FAIL with their reasons and evidence;
- the Tests rows s4r_pose_learning_496250_a2_run and s4r_pose_learning_496250_a2_reading, registered, status written (one diagram label shortened to the registry's 120-character limit first);
- command.json 15a222d1...; owner s4r_pose_learning_owner.py d2e8c84c... (the path step of the logic da57ffb0...); reader read_pose_learning.py 8a0a231c...; source 7dd0eabda; block_draft.json b6a90cb1...; manifest DRAFT cf2abb7e... (80 pins);
- the owner's launch preconditions read statically: 26 PASS, 5 WAIT, 0 REFUSE; the WAITs are the adoption's stop criteria, the declared criteria source, training_preflight check (the adoption file and the binding), package_frozen (the FROZEN manifest) and the binding;
- the 100-model-step and 720 s trainer limits and the closure bound unchanged; the preserved complete 496,250 and its eight worlds read only.

7. THE WORLD-FLUSH WAIT AGAINST THE 178 s RESERVE (independent read-only analysis; no run): NOT A SCHEDULING DEFECT.
- Mechanism: the world flush runs at the end of each captured decision's hold; the trainer reads control.json only when step % 25 == 0, so a flush that takes d seconds delays the stop acknowledgement by d. RECV_TIMEOUT_S = 180 s applies to each worker's answer, not to the whole flush.
- Exact maximum delay to acknowledgement: d + k x pace after the request, k = 0 to 25 model steps to the next read (the owner's admission pace 0.268120 model steps per second; a1's measured 0.340 from its 496,300 record to its acknowledgement). The measured 73.8 s save completes before the cap only when the acknowledgement comes within 104.2 s of the request (178 - 73.8). The owner never runs past the cap: a wall-cap request at cap - 178 s ends the tree at the cap.
- A silent worker: no acknowledgement before the kill at the cap and no complete snapshot whatever the timing (the pool is marked out of step and the worlds' companion cannot be written); the owner records its preservation-risk report; the preserved 496,250 start is untouched. That is an unhealthy run, not a schedule error.
- A slow flush that answers: it needs a disk stall on D:, where every model step already writes synchronously (the live frame and live state each model step). On the lane write costs measured on S4R_measure_496000, the analysis derives about 1.4 s added per 25-step interval, inside the allowance.
- The synthetic durability check did not exercise the world flush across worker processes and guarantees no saving; its record says so.
- Not done, optional: an owner-only larger reserve (no fingerprint change); polling control.json every model step, or skipping the flush once a stop request exists (both trainer code, so a new fingerprint). Proposed bounded checks, not run: the owner's schedule functions on synthetic timelines; observer_flush against stub workers; production-size write times on D:.

NEXT EXECUTABLE ACTION AND DECISIONS (yours):
1. The a2 launch decision: bind the seventh entry's four fields, write the adoption file, set the manifest FROZEN and write the binding receipt, then launch one bounded block; purpose as you stated (bounded learning with durable matched forecasts and actual joints, not the geometry repair).
2. Whether to build the stationarity repair (a module change in _Arm.project's report and the fit, with a test) and rerun C under a new budget.
3. Whether to reword the module's constants comment (item 4).
4. Whether to remove the source branch's RUN_FLAGS line (a source commit and a package rebuild, fingerprint unchanged).
5. Whether to run any of the optional flush checks.

RECORDS: the D1 work item, key pose_objective_build_1341.a2_bounded_arm_check_20261023 (B, C, the analysis, the final package, the next action); main commit 8642c63dd (the record, the four Tests rows, the work record); the design document at 212817d1a.
